findings.title: load() silently parses an existing file with an unsupported extension as delimiter-sniffed CSV, returning garbage instead of an error
findings.description: The load() docstring (step 6) enumerates the supported local-file formats (.geo/pickle, .npy/.npz, .csv/.tsv/.txt, .json, .parquet, .mat, .xlsx/.xls). But a real, existing file with any OTHER extension is not rejected: it falls through to a pandas read_csv with delimiter sniffing, which happily 'parses' arbitrary bytes. A text file containing exactly 'hello' comes back as an empty DataFrame with columns ['he', 'Unnamed: 1', 'o'] (the sniffer picked 'l' as the delimiter) -- no error, no warning. A scientist loading e.g. an instrument's binary/.dat export gets a silently-nonsense DataFrame that flows into downstream analyses. Should raise HypertoolsIOError naming the extension and the supported formats.

p = pathlib.Path('/tmp/junk.xyz'); p.write_text('hello')
print(repr(hyp.load(str(p))))
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError (or ValueError) naming the unsupported extension '.xyz' and listing supported formats
findings.actual:
Empty DataFrame
Columns: [he, Unnamed: 1, o]

findings.title: predict() on empty/degenerate data silently returns nonsense forecasts instead of erroring
findings.description: hyp.predict(np.array([]), t=5) returns a (5, 0) DataFrame -- a '5-step forecast' of zero features from zero observations -- with no error or warning. hyp.predict(5, t=2) likewise returns a (2, 1) 'forecast' from a single scalar observation. Both should raise a clear 'no/too-few observations' error like format_data's 'input has no observations (0 rows)'. (Contrast: hyp.predict([], ...) with an empty LIST crashes in the text pipeline instead -- see finding 005 -- so the two empty forms behave differently, both badly.)

print(hyp.predict(np.array([]), t=5).shape)
print(hyp.predict(5, t=2).shape)
findings.expected: ValueError: input has no observations (or 'need >= 2 observations to forecast')

findings.title: align() and impute() silently swallow misspelled constructor kwargs (documented **kwargs passthrough), returning default-parameter results
findings.description: align's Aligner classes (e.g. HyperAlign.__init__(self, n_iter=10, **kwargs) at hypertools/align/hyperalign.py:114) and impute's wrapper classes (e.g. SimpleImputer.__init__(self, strategy='mean', fill_value=None, **kwargs) at hypertools/impute/sklearn_imputers.py:110) accept arbitrary **kwargs and drop unknown ones. Proven behaviorally: hyp.align([X, Y], n_itr=5) (typo for n_iter) returns output numerically IDENTICAL to the default run, and hyp.impute(XNAN, model='SimpleImputer', stratgy='median') (typo for strategy) returns output identical to default mean-imputation -- while the correctly-spelled kwargs demonstrably change the result (n_iter=0 differs from default; strategy='median' changes imputed cell [2,1] from 0.488704 to 0.568434). The sibling dispatchers behave correctly: hyp.predict(X, model='ARIMA', bogus_kwarg=1) raises "TypeError: ARIMA.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'bogus_kwarg'" and hyp.manip(X, model='Smooth', bogus_kwarg=1) raises the analogous TypeError. A scientist's typo'd analysis parameter is silently ignored in align/impute only.

d = np.asarray(hyp.impute(XNAN, model='SimpleImputer'))

findings.title: Invalid n_clusters leaks sklearn's InvalidParameterError class through cluster()/plot() instead of a hypertools-level ValueError
findings.description: hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=0/-2/2.5/'three') and hyp.plot(X, n_clusters=-2) raise sklearn.utils._param_validation.InvalidParameterError: "The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got 0 instead." The message text is good (sklearn's own), but the exception class is a private sklearn internal (its module is sklearn.utils._param_validation), so callers cannot catch a stable hypertools/builtin class, and it is inconsistent with hypertools' own validated params (ndims -> ValueError, t -> ValueError, resample -> ValueError). n_clusters is a first-class documented hypertools kwarg and deserves hypertools validation.
findings.repro:

hyp.cluster(np.random.rand(20, 4), n_clusters=0)
findings.expected: ValueError: n_clusters must be an integer >= 1; got 0
findings.actual: sklearn.utils._param_validation.InvalidParameterError: The 'n_clusters' parameter of KMeans must be an int in the range [1, inf). Got 0 instead. [sklearn/utils/_param_validation.py:98]

findings.title: ndims larger than the data's feature count is silently capped with no warning (even for explicit PCA); apply_model(ndims=0) silently returns width-0 data

findings.title: save() rough edges: an int fname is treated as an OS file descriptor (OSError Errno 9 -- or a silent write to an unrelated open fd); unpicklable objects raise a bare pickle error; the docstring is a single line
findings.description: hyp.save(X, 42) -> "OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor" -- builtins.open(42, 'wb') interprets the int as a file DESCRIPTOR, so if fd 42 happened to be open (a socket, a log file), the pickle bytes would be written into it silently. hyp.save(lambda..., path) -> raw "AttributeError: Can't get local object '<lambda>.<locals>.<lambda>'" with no 'object is not picklable' context. hyp.save's entire docstring is 'Pickle `obj` to `fname`.' -- it documents neither its **kwargs nor its error behavior, and never mentions that parent directories are not created (FileNotFoundError propagates raw).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.random.rand(3, 3), 42)
findings.expected: TypeError: fname must be a string path; got int
findings.actual: OSError: [Errno 9] Bad file descriptor [io/save.py:21]; save(<lambda>, path) -> AttributeError: Can't get local object '<lambda>.<locals>.<lambda>' [io/save.py:22]

hyp.impute(np.full((10, 3), np.nan))

findings.actual: ValueError: zero-size array to reduction operation maximum which has no identity [numpy/_core/fromnumeric.py:86]
